They are large humanoid [[Fairy|Fairies]].https://zelda.com/about/ Their main purpose is to heal [[Link]] whenever he is wounded. They will also recover his [[Magic Meter]] in games that incorporate one. In other titles, such as {{OoT}} and {{TWW}}, they also bless Link with new items, powers, or upgrades of his existing equipment. Most Great Fairies can be found living within a [[Great Fairy Fountain]]. {{Terminology |- | {{Term/Store|Great Fairy|Great Fairies|Series, ALttP, LANS, OoT, OoT3D, MM, MM3D, FS, TWW, TWWHD, TMC, TP, TPHD, BotW, TotK, EoW, HWDE}} | {{List| * {{ALttP}} * {{LANS}} * {{OoT}} * {{OoT3D}} * {{MM}} * {{MM3D}} * {{FS}} * {{TWW}} * {{TWWHD}} * {{TMC}} * {{TP}} * {{TPHD}} * {{BotW}} * {{TotK}} * {{EoW}} * {{HWDE}} }} |- | '''Guardian Spirits''' | {{BotW}} }} ==Biography== ==={{TLoZ|-}}=== In {{TLoZ}}, while not specifically referred to as a Great Fairy, and appearing as a normal [[Fairy]], there are a few ponds in the [[Hyrule]] overworld where they can be found. These pool-dwelling Fairies have the same role as Great Fairies in later games; they will only appear if Link approaches their pond with less than full health, and will instantly recover all of his [[Heart]]s. ==={{ALttP|-}}=== In {{ALttP}}, Great Fairies can easily be found scattered throughout Hyrule in either caves or holes. When Link approaches one, she will completely heal his wounds. Great Fairies seem able to maintain their normal forms even while in the [[Dark World]], despite its corrupting effects. At the [[Waterfall of Wishing]] near [[Zora's Waterfall]] lives a Great Fairy who is known to be a friend of [[Venus]].{{Cite|I cannot grant any more wishes for you, but a friend of mine might be able to... She lives in the Waterfall Of Wishing near Zora's lake. I will return your Rupees to you. May you be happy...|Venus|ALttP}} She looks identical to Venus with the exception of her wings, which are smaller and more green. The Fairy at the Waterfall of Wishing appears when Link throws various items into the [[Mysterious Pond]] and will ask him if he was the one who dropped them. She will return any item thrown by the hero, but if he drops certain items, she will instead give him better items or upgrades of the item if Link answers her questions honestly.{{Cite|Hello there. Did you drop this? I like an honest person. I will give you something better in return.|Great Fairy|ALttP}} These include the [[Boomerang]], which she upgrades to the [[Magical Boomerang]], the blue Level-1 [[Fighter's Shield]], which she upgrades to the [[Red Shield]], and a [[Bottle]], which she fills with [[Medicine of Magic]]. ==={{LA|-}}=== In {{LA}}, Great Fairies are found scattered throughout certain areas of [[Koholint Island]], usually in a cave that houses a small pond and two Fairy statues. They heal Link's wounds when approached. Not all Great Fairies in {{LA|-}} live in a cave, there is one that lives in a small pond in the [[Mysterious Woods]]. There is also the [[Fairy Queen]] who only makes an appearance in {{LADX}}, and resides in the last room of the [[Color Dungeon]], a dungeon exclusive to {{LADX|-}}. As thanks for visiting her, she rewards Link with the "power of color"; a choice between the [[Red Clothes]], which increases Link's attack power, or the [[Blue Clothes]], which increases Link's defense.{{Cite|Welcome, Link . I admire you for coming this far. I will give you the power of color. If you want offense, choose red. If you want defense choose blue. Which power do you want?|Great Fairy|LADX}} Link can visit the Fairy Queen again to swap between the two tunics, but he can never get his green tunic back once he has swapped it for another tunic. ==={{OoT|-}}=== In {{OoT}}, Great Fairies are depicted as giant women who wear ivy vines and leather boots for clothing, and have red hair that is tied into three pigtails. This also marks the first time that Great Fairies are seen without wings. Their locations are scattered throughout Hyrule, where they live in certain Great Fairy Fountains that all have the [[Triforce]] symbol engraved on the floor in front of their pond. By playing "[[Zelda's Lullaby]]" on this symbol, the fountain's Great Fairy will be summoned. Great Fairies, when first called, will bless Link with either a new item or an upgrade. The color of their fountain's walls also vary from either blue or red to signify what kind of blessing they will give. Three of the Great Fairies give out [[Din's Fire]], [[Nayru's Love]] and [[Farore's Wind]]. Another three will upgrade Link's abilities, giving him the [[Spin Attack|Magic Spin Attack]] and the Magic Meter, a larger Magic Meter, and doubled defense in the form of an extended health bar. The Great Fairies can also be summoned again at their fountains to recover Link's health as well as his Magic Meter. All three of the Great Fairies who give out Din's Fire, Nayru's Love and Farore's Wind refer to themselves as the Great Fairy of Magic,{{Cite|Welcome Link! I am the Great Fairy of Magic! I will give you a magic spell. Please take it.|Great Fairy of Magic|OoT}} and possibly may be the same Great Fairy. The Great Fairies who bless Link with a magical sword spin attack, a larger Magic Meter, and a defense upgrade are referred to as the Great Fairy of Power,{{Cite|I am the Great Fairy of Power! I'm going to grant you a sword technique. Receive it now!|Great Fairy of Power|OoT}} the Great Fairy of Wisdom,{{Cite|Welcome Link! I am the Great Fairy of Wisdom! I'm going to enhance your magic power. Receive it now!|Great Fairy of Wisdom|OoT}} and the Great Fairy of Courage, respectively.{{Cite|Welcome Link! I am the Great Fairy of Courage! I'm going to enhance your defensive power. Five Great Fairies appear in [[Termina]], all having been torn apart into 15 [[Stray Fairy|Stray Fairies]] by the evil power of [[Majora's Mask (Item)|Majora's Mask]]. The only Great Fairy that needs to be restored in order to progress in the game is the one in [[North Clock Town]], who grants Link the ability to use Magic, and only one Stray Fairy has to be found for her to once again be complete. Near the [[Eyeglass Island Library]] in the past, Link encounters the [[Fairy Queen]], guardian of the [[Zora Seas]], who was cursed by [[Veran]] into an [[Octorok]]-shape so that the evil sorceress could poison the seas and kill the [[Zora]]s without the Fairy Queen's interference.{{Cite|Please listen, young one! You may not believe this, but I am the Queen Fairy, guardian of this sea! The curse of an evil one named Veran has made me appear so!|Fairy Queen|OoA}} She asks Link to find the [[Fairy Powder]] hidden in the nearby Library to heal her,{{Cite|The magic of Fairy Powder can turn me back to normal. Veran has poisoned the sea. Soon all living things in it will perish! Please go find some Fairy Powder!|Fairy Queen|OoA}} and once he does, she cleanses the pollution from the sea, returning its natural beauty and restoring health to the [[King Zora]] and [[Lord Jabu-Jabu]].{{Cite|You brought me Fairy Powder! Now I can return to normal! Sprinkle the powder on me! Thank you, young one! Now I can cleanse the seas of evil!|Fairy Queen|OoA}}{{Cite|The seas are back to normal! King Zora is all better, too! All is good!|Zora|OoA}}{{Cite|Thanks to you, our seawater is clean again, and Jabu-Jabu's health has returned.|King Zora|OoA}} ==={{FS|-}}=== In {{FS}}, three Great Fairies act as the guardians of the [[Sea of Trees]], [[Talus Cave]], and [[Death Mountain]]. After completing each [[Stage]] with the appropriate amount of [[Rupee]]s, the respective Great Fairy will award the [[Links]] with a key to unlock [[Vaati's Palace]].{{Cite Book|quote= |book= E |publisher= |page= 23{{Exp Game|FS}}}} In {{FSAE}}, completing the [[Hero's Key]] door in Vaati's Palace causes the Great Fairies' appearance and personality to change and resemble the Great Fairies from {{MM}}.{{Cite|Welcome! You have done well to get this far. I am the Great Fairy of Forest! Throughout the ages I have listened to the whispering of these woods as the guardian of the Sea of Trees.|Great Fairy of Forest|FSAE}}{{Cite|I see you already have the three {{Color FS|Orange|Hero Keys}}! I wonder if you know about the path that opened to {{Color FS|Blue|Vaati's Palace}}. It has {{Color FS|Orange|12 floors}}... Do you need an explanation? ...No? Then off you go, brave heroes!|Great Fairy of Forest|FSAE}} {|class="wikitable" |+Locations |- !Name !Location !Image !Alt Image{{Exp|{{FSAE|-}}, after completing Hero's door in Vaati's Palace}} |- |[[Great Fairy of Forest]] |[[Sea of Trees]] |[[File:FS Great Fairy of Forest Sprite.png|100px]] |[[File:FSAE Great Fairy of Forest Post Game Sprite.png|100px]] |- |[[Great Fairy of Ice]] |[[Talus Cave]] |[[File:FS Great Fairy of Ice Sprite.png|100px]] |[[File:FSAE Great Fairy of Ice Post Game Sprite.png|100px]] |- |[[Great Fairy of Flame]] |[[Death Mountain]] |[[File:FS Great Fairy of Flame Sprite.png|100px]] |[[File:FSAE Great Fairy of Flame Post Game Sprite.png|100px]] |} ==={{TWW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= TWW |type= Characters |category= Characters in The Wind Waker |needs= * Detailed information on the character's role in the story, including what quests they are involved in * Detailed information on where the character lives and travels to }} {{Descriptions TWW}} In {{TWW}}, there are seven Great Fairies, five of which reside in fountains under a giant shell. They have dark skins, light hairstyles and dresses and have four arms. One must be rescued from inside a [[Big Octo]] at [[Two-Eye Reef]].{{Cite|I tell you, lately no one around these waters has seen the beautiful fairy who bestows magic power. She used to live here, fry. All anyone ever sees anymore are the Big Octos that have been appearing lately. Maybe they scared her off... Oh no! I sure hope...they didn't eat her!|Fishman|TWW}} Another Great Fairy, the Fortune Goddess,{{Cite|It was also said that whoever met with the Great Fairy who lived here was blessed with great fortune, so it came to be known as the Fountain of the Fortune Goddess.|N/A|TWW}} lives in the [[Forest of Fairies]] in [[Outset Island]] and gives Link a larger [[Wallet]]. The upgrades received, along with the names of the islands in which the Great Fairies are located, are as follows: *'''Pink Great Fairy''': Wallet upgrade. :*[[Northern Fairy Island]] – There is no obstacle blocking the entrance; this fountain can be visited as soon as the [[Forbidden Woods]] have been completed. :*[[Outset Island]] in the [[Fairy Forest]] – A bomb must be used to blow up the rock blocking the entrance. *'''Blue Great Fairy''': [[Bomb Bag]] upgrade. :*[[Eastern Fairy Island]] – A bomb must be used to blow up the rock blocking the entrance. :*[[Southern Fairy Island]] – A bomb or a Fire Arrow must be used to destroy the wooden wall blocking the entrance. *'''Violet Great Fairy''': [[Magic Meter]] upgrade :*[[Two-Eye Reef]] – A [[Big Octo]] must be defeated to rescue the Great Fairy. *'''Yellow Great Fairy''': [[Quiver]] upgrade: :*[[Western Fairy Island]] – The Skull Hammer must be used to hit the nearby stake and remove the fire blocking the entrance. :*[[Thorned Fairy Island]] – The Skull Hammer must be used to hit the three nearby stakes and remove the thorns blocking the entrance. After granting Link their respective upgrades, the Great Fairies subsequently vanish from their fountains, leaving in their place a handful of healing fairies, which Link can also capture in [[Bottle]]s for later use. ==={{FSA|-}}=== In {{FSA}}, Link can encounter a Great Fairy while inside certain dungeons or caves. If Link throws in a certain item into the Great Fairy's pond, she will upgrade it to a Level 2 item. For example, throwing in the [[Slingshot]] will allow Link to shoot seeds from three different directions at the same time. Encountering these Great Fairies is crucial in order to solve various [[puzzle]]s within the stages. The [[Fairy Queen]] also appears in {{FSA|-}}, during the [[Hyrule Castle (Dungeon)|Hyrule Castle]] level. ==={{TMC|-}}=== {{Main|Great Butterfly Fairy, Great Dragonfly Fairy, Great Mayfly Fairy}} Three Great Fairies appear in {{TMC}}, each one found in a [[Great Fairy Fountain]] hidden in [[Hyrule]]. Their appearances are based off different [[Insect]]s. They each test Link in a different manner and reward him if he passes. ==={{TP|-}}=== In {{TP}}, a Great Fairy appears within the [[Cave of Ordeals]] in the fountains that are found every ten floors. Each time Link reaches a new fountain, the Great Fairy will send healing Fairies to one of the [[Spirit Spring]]s across [[Hyrule]].{{Cite|In praise of your efforts thus far, I will release fairies to {{Color TPHD|Red|Ordon Spring}}.|Great Fairy|TPHD}} The first time Link reaches the fountain on the 50th floor, the Great Fairy will reward him by filling one of the young hero's [[Empty Bottle]]s with [[Great Fairy's Tears]].{{Cite|You cleared many ordeals... How impressive. In praise of your courage, I will give you this blessing.|Great Fairy|TPHD}} She will also tell him that he can get more Tears by going to any of the Light Spirit's Springs, although Link will only be able to have one Bottle filled with Great Fairy's Tears at any given time.{{Cite|If ever you need my assistance again, visit any {{Color TPHD|Red|spring}}.|Great Fairy|TPHD}} However, should he complete the Cave of Ordeals again, he will be able to fill another Bottle with the Tears at the fountain on the 50th floor, allowing him to have more than one.{{Fact}} The Great Fairy can also warp Link out of the Cave of Ordeals, should he ask. ==={{ALBW|-}}=== In {{ALBW}}, Great Fairies are commonly found scattered throughout the land of Hyrule. Many of them can be found in the same places as the previous Great Fairies. These Great Fairies will completely heal Link every time they are visited. The [[Great Rupee Fairy]] is found in [[Lorule]], in a cave behind the [[Bomb Flower Store]]. Once [[Link]] has access to the [[Big Bomb Flower]], the entrance to her fountain can be opened by blowing up the large rock in front of it. ==={{BotW|-}}=== In {{BotW}} only four Great Fairies appear, named [[Cotera]], [[Kaysa]], [[Mija]] and [[Tera]]. At first they are found in closed [[Great Fairy Fountain#Breath of the Wild|Great Fairy Fountain]]s resembling a large flower bud. To restore them, Link must offer them an increasing amount of Rupees. Once restored they will upgrade Link's [[Armor#Breath of the Wild|Armor]] when provided with the proper [[Material#Breath of the Wild|Materials]], though the max level depends on the total number of restored Fairies. Additionally, a fifth Fairy Fountain can be found, but it contains the Horse God [[Malanya]] instead, though his hands resemble those of a Great Fairy. ==={{TotK|-}}=== {{Stub|TotK}} The same four Great Fairies return in {{TotK}}. Their [[Great Fairy Fountain#Tears of the Kingdom|Great Fairy Fountain]]s have moved to be closer to [[Stable]]s, and they have reverted to a bulb like state as the Great Fairies hide inside them. To restore them, Link must bring the [[Stable Trotters]] to perform for them in a series of [[Side Adventure#Serenade to a Great Fairy|Side Adventures]]. Once restored, the Great Fairies will reprise their role of upgrading Link's [[Armor#Tears of the Kingdom|Armor]]. ==={{EoW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= EoW |type= Characters |category= Characters in Echoes of Wisdom |needs= * Detailed information on the character's role in the story, including what quests they are involved in * Detailed information on where the character lives and travels to }} {{Quests| {{EoW Quest |name= The Great Fairy's Request |type= Side Quest |location= [[Great Fairy Shrine]] }} }} {{Stub|EoW}} The Great Fairy resides within the [[Great Fairy Shrine]] on [[Lake Hylia]]. She has the ability to upgrade the amount of [[Accessory|Accessories]] [[Princess Zelda]] is able to wear at once in exchange for [[Rupee]]s. The list of upgrades and their costs are as follows: {{Data Table Copy |fromPage= Great Fairy Shrine |storedAs= Accessory Slots }} ==Other Appearances== ==={{SSBB|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} The Great Fairy from {{TWW|-}} appears as a [[Trophy (Super Smash Bros.)|Trophy]] and a [[Sticker]] in {{SSBB}}. ====Trophy Information==== {{SSBTrophy|SSBB|header=yes}} {{#section:Trophies in Super Smash Bros. Brawl|Great Fairy}} |} ====Sticker Information==== {{SSBSticker|header=yes}} {{#section:Sticker|Great Fairy}} |} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{HW|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Main|Great Fairy (Item)}} [[File:HW Great Fountain Fairy Render.png|200px|right|The Great Fairy, with Link in a bottle, in {{HW|-}}]] In {{HW}}, Great Fairies appear in several Scenarios, heavily modeled on the {{OoT|-}} incarnation. They are supportive characters who live inside [[Fairy Fountain]]s, and they may be summoned by praying to them for aid inside of [[Magic Circle]]s. They help in various ways, depending on the battle; such as sending Fairies to drop giant Bombs on enemy units, calling upon a recreation of the Terminian [[Moon (Object)|Moon]] to knock [[Argorok]] out of the sky, or sending a rain of energy that destroys several enemies on the field. Great Fairies appear in [[Hyrule Field (Stage)|Hyrule Field]], [[Faron Woods (Stage)|Faron Woods]], [[Valley of Seers]], [[Palace of Twilight (Stage)|Palace of Twilight]], and [[Skyloft (Stage)|Skyloft]], where their fountains can be found. Whether they are summoned or not depends on the Scenario. [[Great Fairy (Item)|Great Fairies]] are also a class of Weapon used by Link, in which control switches to the Great Fairy (as the Weapon) while Link is kept inside of a giant Bottle. The kind of Great Fairy that appears depends on the level of Weapon used. The Great Fairy uses magic attacks and magically-enhanced physical attacks in battle. In some combo attacks, Link is momentarily released as he and the Great Fairy perform special, combined attacks, including a form of [[Dead Man's Volley]] that targets surrounding enemies. The Great Fairy's enormous size makes her a powerful character, and her attacks cover a wide range. The Great Fairy Weapon is of the Water [[Element]]. In the {{BP}} [[Downloadable Content]] Pack and in {{HWDE}}, Great Fairies appear as [[Giant Boss]]es that are fought in [[Ganon's Fury]] mode. They appear in battles acting as healers to other Giant Bosses that Ganon fights. They must first be defeated in order to prevent the other Bosses from recovering. They continue to carry giant [[Empty Bottle]]s, although with Link absent, and do not perform any attacks that require both the Great Fairy and Link. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{SSBU|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Spirits}} In {{SSBU}}, the Great Fairy appears as a [[Spirit]] with the skill, Critical-Health Healing, which heals the user when they reach high damage. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoC|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Improve}} In {{AoC}}, the four sister Great Fairies from {{BotW|-}}; Cotera, Tera, Kaysa, and Mija, as well as Malanya, fight as a single [[Warrior]] by all sharing the same bud and use their magic bangles as their Weapon.{{Cite|Four sisters called Tera, Kaysa, Mija, and Cotera. They are residents of secret fountains hidden across Hyrule. They have temporarily gathered in a single bud to aid Link.|Game Screen|AoC}} They will change places with each other as they attack, and their unique action is dependent on which of the Great Fairies is currently active. The Great Fairies can be unlocked after completing the [[Scenario]], "[[Akkala Tower (Scenario)|Akkala Tower]]", where the first [[Side Quest]] necessary to unlock the Great Fairies, "[[Offering Help on the Road]]", will begin. After this, the four [[Challenge]]s necessary to unlock the Great Fairies will be unlocked. They are: "[[Fairy Fountain: Grassy Plains]]", "[[Fairy Fountain: Deep Snows]]", "[[Fairy Fountain: Desert Sands]]", and "[[Fairy Fountain: Battlefield]]". {{Noncanon|End}} ==Trivia== * There is an error in the Great Fairies' names in {{MM|-}}. The Great Fairy found in [[Snowhead Temple]] introduces herself as the Great Fairy of Wisdom and then as the Great Fairy of Courage on subsequent visits. Likewise, the Great Fairy near the [[Great Bay Coast]] says she is the Great Fairy of Courage and then the Great Fairy of Wisdom. ** It is possible that the two Great Fairies addressed themselves with the wrong titles in their first introductions, as the green-haired Great Fairy's name is colored indigo and the purple-haired Great Fairy's name is colored green, whilst both the names of the Great Fairy of Power and the Great Fairy of Kindness are colored to match each of their hair. However, {{MM3D|-}} kept the same dialogues. * In American English, British English, German, and Italian versions of {{TWW|-}}, the birthplace of the Great Fairies are stated as [[Angular Isles]] in their Figurine descriptions. It is a mistranslation of "{{Romanize|かく島々|Kaku Shima-jima||3}}", which means "varied islands", and is presumably confused with Angular Isles' Japanese name, "{{Romanize|カクカク島|Kakukaku-Shima||3}}".
